blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: The case study this topic requires: a rapidly growing urban area in a developing country and the migration to it, told through Lagos in Nigeria.

blocks.heading: The growth of Lagos
blocks.text: Lagos, on Nigeria's coast, is one of the largest cities in Africa, with an estimated 16.5 million people in 2024 and growth of hundreds of thousands a year, so a city the size of Namibia's whole population arrives every few years. It was Nigeria's capital until 1991 and remains the country's chief port and commercial city: the port at Apapa, the factories and markets around it and the office towers of Victoria Island draw workers, and migrants arrive from the rural north and east of Nigeria and from neighbouring countries for what a city sells, wages, secondary schools and hospitals. The growth has outpaced the services, and housing, water and traffic all fall short of the arrivals, which is what the second block shows.

blocks.heading: The impacts and the answers, by name
blocks.text: The impacts are specific and named. Makoko is the best known: a settlement of houses on stilts above the lagoon, where thousands of families live without secure land or piped water, and where daily life runs on canoes through the channels between the houses. The city's traffic is heavy, and the Bus Rapid Transit system, launched in 2008, carries commuters in dedicated lanes to ease it. On the Atlantic side, Eko Atlantic is a new district on land reclaimed from the sea behind a long sea wall, adding office and apartment ground the old city has none of. Together they show both kinds of answer at work: serving the people the growth has already brought, with taps and transit, and building the ground the growth will need, which is the two-part answer an urban-growth question rewards. A case-study answer names the city, the districts and the schemes, and lets the places carry the argument.

blocks.heading: Where this connects
blocks.text: Lagos's migration is topic 1.2's push and pull in one place; Makoko and the 2008 transit system are topic 1.6's problems and solutions at a developing-country scale.
